events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Southern Kenai Mtns
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Snow. Additional snow accumulations between 1 and 4 inches.
Winds gusting as high as 20 mph.

* WHERE...Seward.

* WHEN...Until 3 AM AKST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Roads, and especially
bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous. Ice
accumulations could lead to power outages.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Lingering cold air is keeping precipitation
all snow. As such, the Advisory has been extended again.
Precipitation will very likely change over to rain overnight,
though there remains a 25 to 35 percent chance for a brief period
of freezing rain during this transition period.

grouped_sources.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Anchorage; Anchorage Hillside / Eagle River
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Freezing rain and mixed precipitation expected. Ice
accumulations around a light glaze. Additional snow amounts of up
to 1 inch.

* WHERE...Anchorage / Eagle River (all elevations).

* WHEN...Until 3 AM AKST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Roads, and especially
bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous. The
combination of snow and light ice accumulations may result in a few
localized power outages.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Steady snow has transitioned into snow/rain
showers. As surface temperatures currently range from 20 to 30
degrees, any falling rain may freeze on contact and create icy
surfaces.

grouped_sources.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: East Turnagain Arm; Portage
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Additional snow accumulations
up to 2 inches and ice accumulations around a light glaze.

* WHERE...East Turnagain Arm, including Portage Valley and Girdwood.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM AKST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Roads, and especially
bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
Light ice accumulations may result in a few localized power
outages.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Warm air aloft is transitioning snow to rain
showers. As surface temperatures are below freezing in many
locations, falling rain may freeze on contact and create icy
surfaces. Surface temperatures are unlikely to warm above freezing
overnight, so the Advisory has been extended to Monday afternoon,
when surface temperatures will be warm enough to end the threat of
icing from freezing rain.
